extension.evidence.flagged_dangerous: Google Safe Browsing — the list Chrome, Firefox and Safari use to warn people — marks this site as unsafe.
extension.evidence.flagged_phishing: This site is in anti-phishing databases — lists of sites that trick people out of passwords or card details.
extension.evidence.on_blocklists: Security researchers have already put this site on lists of scam and spam sites.
extension.evidence.threat_reports: Security researchers mention this site in their reports about attacks.
extension.evidence.spreads_malware: This site has been caught spreading programs that infect computers and phones.
extension.evidence.imitates_brand: The address looks like a well-known company's, but it doesn't belong to that company.
extension.evidence.lookalike_letters: Some letters in the address only look like ordinary ones. That is how the real address is hidden.
extension.evidence.fake_brand_address: A famous name sits at the start of the address, but the site itself belongs to someone else.
extension.evidence.copies_brand_icon: The page shows a real company's icon but lives at an unrelated address — a common trick for stealing logins.
extension.evidence.no_https: Anything you type on this site is sent without protection and can be intercepted.
extension.evidence.missing_protections: The site skips basic protections that real companies normally set up.
extension.evidence.raw_ip_address: Real companies give their sites a name. Scam pages often use a bare number instead.
extension.evidence.unusual_connection: The site uses an unusual way to connect that ordinary websites rarely need.
extension.evidence.hidden_destination: The link hides the address it really leads to.
extension.evidence.very_new_site: Scam sites usually live just a few days, so a brand-new address is a warning sign.
extension.evidence.scam_words: The address contains words like “login” or “secure” that scammers add to look official.
extension.evidence.carries_personal_data: The link itself carries your email or a sign-in key. Anyone who sees the link can take them.
extension.evidence.long_complex_address: The address is long and tangled, so it's hard to see where it really leads.
extension.evidence.many_redirects: The link is built to pass you on to another address — often a way to hide where it really goes.
extension.evidence.risky_ending: The address ends in a zone (like .xyz or .top) where scam sites are especially common.
extension.evidence.risky_registrar: The site was registered through a service that scammers often choose.
extension.evidence.random_name: The name looks like a random jumble — typical of sites churned out for one-off scams.
extension.evidence.detector_suspicious: Our detector, trained on thousands of real and scam sites, finds this one similar to the scams.
extension.evidence.not_a_real_business: The site has no working email. Real companies almost always do.
extension.evidence.shifty_setup: The site's address can switch between many servers very quickly. Large services do this too, but scam networks use it so their sites are harder to shut down.
extension.evidence.padded_address: Extra parts are stacked in front of the real name so it's hard to spot.
extension.evidence.shared_hosting: Anyone can make a site on this service in minutes, scammers included.
extension.evidence.on_cleanway_list: Cleanway's own list of known scam sites includes this one.
extension.evidence.site_not_found: There is no working site at this address right now. Check the spelling.
extension.evidence.unreachable_abroad: Our server abroad couldn't open this site, so the page itself wasn't checked.
extension.evidence.checks_incomplete: Not every check finished in time, so this verdict rests on fewer signs.
extension.evidence.user_content_platform: Anyone can publish pages on this service. We can't vouch for this particular page.
extension.evidence.invalid_address: The address itself is broken. It may be a trap set for people who copy links.
extension.evidence.private_network: Ordinary public websites don't lead there, so we didn't open it.
extension.evidence.ai_second_look: When the signs point both ways, an AI model reviews them and may adjust the verdict a little.
extension.evidence.well_known_site: This is one of the well-known sites we recognize as genuine.
extension.evidence.popular_site: This site is on the list of the world's most visited sites. That counts in its favor, but other warning signs still matter.
extension.evidence.detector_safe: Our detector, trained on thousands of real and scam sites, finds this one similar to real sites.
extension.evidence.on_your_trusted_list: You added this site to your trusted sites yourself.
extension.evidence.high_risk_score: A service that rates sites for fraud gives this one a high risk score. That is an estimate, not a confirmed report.
extension.evidence.new_certificate: Scam sites often appear with a brand-new certificate. Real sites renew theirs regularly too, so on its own this means little.
extension.evidence.broken_certificate: The certificate that proves who runs this site has expired, was not issued by a trusted authority, or belongs to another address. Your browser will warn about it too.

extension.webmail.setting_label: Scan emails I open in Gmail, Outlook and Yahoo for phishing
extension.webmail.setting_consent: Off unless you turn it on. When on, every email you open in Gmail, Outlook or Yahoo Mail is sent to Cleanway's server (api.cleanway.ai) to be checked for phishing: its subject, the sender's name and address, the Reply-To address, the text of the message, and the address and text of each link in it. The email is checked and not stored; the domains of its links are also checked with Google Safe Browsing. Turn this off at any time and scanning stops at once.

mobile.home.check.title: Check anything
mobile.home.check.desc: Paste a link, scan a QR code, or share anything suspicious straight to Cleanway
mobile.home.check.share_sheet_body: From any app, tap Share, then choose Cleanway. We'll check the link and tell you if it's safe.
mobile.home.check.note: Works with anything you can copy or share — including iMessage.
mobile.home.check.note_android: Works with anything you can copy or share — links, texts and messenger chats.
mobile.home.check.share_sheet_body_ios: In any app, tap Share, then Cleanway. Don't see it? Scroll the row of apps to the end, tap More and add Cleanway.
mobile.home.sms_check.title: SMS check
mobile.home.sms_check.desc: Got a suspicious SMS? Send it to Cleanway: press and hold the message → Share → Cleanway. Or paste the text.
mobile.home.sms_check.honesty: Cleanway doesn't read your SMS on its own — it checks only the message you give it. The text stays on your phone.
mobile.home.sms_check.links_on: Links in SMS are also checked when you tap them: known scam sites won't open.

mobile.home.activity.hint: Tap a number to see the list.
mobile.home.privacy: The “All apps” shield matches website names on your phone. When you check a link yourself, or tap one with “Link checking” on, our server gets the website name and a random install number that changes every day.
mobile.home.interrupted: Your phone stopped protection — for example after a restart, or to save battery. Your setup is still here: tap the button below, then "{{button}}".
mobile.home.interrupted_private_dns: Protection stopped because of the "Private DNS" setting. That setting no longer gets in the way: tap the button below, then "{{button}}".

With DNS protection on, it also gets the names of the sites your iPhone opens, without recording who opened what. Message texts and full page addresses never leave your phone.

mobile.keep_alive.title: Keep protection on
mobile.keep_alive.intro: Phones stop apps in the background to save battery — and Cleanway's protection with them, without a word. These steps keep it running when the app is closed.
mobile.keep_alive.all_set: Everything your phone reports is set. Protection keeps running when the app is closed.
mobile.keep_alive.running_unproven: Protection is running, not confirmed yet

mobile.keep_alive.battery_explain_title: Let protection run in the background
mobile.keep_alive.battery_explain_body:
To save battery, Android can stop apps that work in the background — and Cleanway's protection with them, without telling you. Protection uses very little battery: it only looks at website names.

On the next screen, tap "Allow". If a list of apps opens instead, find Cleanway and choose "Don't optimise" or "Unrestricted".
mobile.keep_alive.oem_note: Cleanway can't see this setting, so it can't tick it for you. Doing it once is enough.
mobile.keep_alive.oem_row_samsung: Samsung: keep Cleanway out of sleeping apps
mobile.keep_alive.oem_title_samsung: Samsung: never put Cleanway to sleep
mobile.keep_alive.oem_steps_samsung:
1. Open Settings → Battery (or Device care → Battery).
2. Tap "Background usage limits".
3. Open "Never sleeping apps" and add Cleanway.
4. Check that Cleanway is not in "Sleeping apps" or "Deep sleeping apps".
mobile.keep_alive.oem_title_xiaomi: Xiaomi, Redmi, POCO: let Cleanway start by itself
mobile.keep_alive.oem_steps_xiaomi:
1. On the screen that opens, turn on Autostart for Cleanway.
2. Then open Settings → Apps → Cleanway → Battery saver and choose "No restrictions".
mobile.keep_alive.oem_row_huawei: Huawei / Honor: let Cleanway run in the background
mobile.keep_alive.oem_title_huawei: Huawei, Honor: manage Cleanway's launch by hand
mobile.keep_alive.oem_steps_huawei:
1. Open Settings → Battery → App launch.
2. Find Cleanway and switch off "Manage automatically".
3. In the window that opens, leave Auto-launch, Secondary launch and Run in background on.
mobile.keep_alive.oem_row_oppo: OPPO / realme / OnePlus: allow background activity
mobile.keep_alive.oem_title_oppo: OPPO, realme, OnePlus: let Cleanway run in the background
mobile.keep_alive.oem_steps_oppo:
1. Open Settings → Apps → Cleanway → Battery usage (or Battery).
2. Turn on "Allow background activity" and "Allow auto launch".
3. If there is a "Startup manager" or "Auto launch" list, turn Cleanway on there too.
mobile.keep_alive.oem_row_vivo: vivo / iQOO: allow background power use
mobile.keep_alive.oem_title_vivo: vivo, iQOO: let Cleanway run in the background
mobile.keep_alive.oem_steps_vivo:
1. Open Settings → Battery → Background power consumption management.
2. Find Cleanway and choose "Allow".
3. If your phone has Autostart (i Manager → App manager), turn it on for Cleanway.
mobile.rollout.network_ios: Blocks scam sites in almost every app. In final testing — not on iPhone yet.
mobile.rollout.browser_ios: Warns you right on the page in Safari. Coming next.
mobile.rollout.messages_ios: Filters scam texts (SMS). Planned — it will never be able to see iMessage.
mobile.rollout.browser_android: Checks links you tap in any app, before they open. Coming next.
mobile.rollout.messages_android: Needs a newer version of the app. You can already check a link from a text: Share → Cleanway.
mobile.check.title: Check a link
mobile.check.subtitle: Paste any link or type a website name
mobile.check.placeholder: example.com or paste a full link
mobile.check.invalid_title: That doesn't look like a link
mobile.check.invalid_body: Type a website name like example.com, or paste the whole link.
mobile.scanner.permission_body: Cleanway uses the camera only to read QR codes. Nothing is recorded and no picture is saved.
mobile.scanner.permission_blocked_body: Camera access is switched off for Cleanway. Open Settings to switch it back on — the camera is only used to read QR codes.
mobile.scanner.instruction: Point the camera at a QR code
mobile.scanner.instruction_sub: Hold steady until the code sits inside the frame
mobile.scanner.no_link_body: This QR code does not contain a website link, so there is nothing to check.
mobile.scanner.privacy: The code is read on your phone. To check it, only the website name and a random install number that changes every day go to our servers.
mobile.result.low_confidence: Limited analysis — some checks couldn't run
mobile.result.privacy: Checked on our servers. Only the website name and a random install number that changes every day were sent. Nothing tied to your name or phone number.
mobile.result.error_body: The server didn't answer. Check your connection and try again.
mobile.result.error_rate_limited: Too many checks right now — from this phone or from your network. Wait a couple of minutes and try again.
mobile.result.error_server: Our server had a problem, not your connection. Please try again in a minute.
mobile.result.listed_title: Dangerous — this site is on the list of scam sites
mobile.result.listed_reason: This site is on the list of scam sites on your phone
mobile.result.details_failed: Couldn't load details from our server. But the site is already on the scam list — don't open it.
mobile.result.listed_server_calm: Our server found nothing else, but the site is on the list of scam sites — don't open it.
mobile.result.error_slow: Our server is answering slowly. Please try again in a minute.
mobile.result.not_found_title: This site doesn't exist — check the address
mobile.result.not_found_body: There may be a typo in the address, or the site has already been taken down. If the link came in a message, don't trust that message.
mobile.result.privacy_listed: Found in the list on this phone. For details we ask our server, which gets only the website name and a random install number that changes every day.
mobile.shared.score_caption: Risk score — higher means more suspicious
mobile.shared.advice_safe: We found no problems with this website name.
mobile.shared.advice_caution: Something looks off. Don't sign in or pay on this site until you're sure.
mobile.shared.advice_dangerous: Don't open this link. Never type your password or card details there.
mobile.shared.no_url_body: Nothing came through, or what was shared wasn't a link. Try sharing it again.
mobile.shared.check_failed_body: We couldn't reach our servers, so we don't know if this link is safe. Please try again in a moment.
mobile.shared.no_browser: There's no other browser on this phone to open the link. Install one, or open it manually.
mobile.message.title: Check a text message
mobile.message.subtitle: Copy the suspicious message and paste it here. Or, in your messages app, press and hold the message → Share → Cleanway.
mobile.message.placeholder: Paste the text of the SMS
mobile.message.paste_empty: Nothing is copied yet. Press and hold the message, choose Copy, then come back here.
mobile.message.checking_sub: Right here on your phone — the text is not sent anywhere.
mobile.message.verdict_sub.dangerous: This message uses scammers' tricks. Don't do what it asks.
mobile.message.verdict_sub.caution: Something here is suspicious. Don't rush — check it yourself first.
mobile.message.verdict_sub.no_signals: We found none of the usual scam tricks. That's not a guarantee — stay alert.
mobile.message.verdict_sub.checking_link: We found no scam tricks in the text. Wait until we have checked the links — and don't open them before that.
mobile.message.verdict_sub.links_uncheck: We found no scam tricks in the text, but we did not check the site the link leads to — see the list below. Don't open the link unless you're sure who sent the message.
mobile.message.reason.link_blocklisted: The link leads to a site on our list of scam sites
mobile.message.reason.link_checked_dange: Our check found the site in the link dangerous
mobile.message.reason.link_checked_cauti: The site in the link looks suspicious
mobile.message.reason.claims_organisatio: It claims to be from a bank, a government service or another organisation
mobile.message.reason.threat_or_urgency: It scares or rushes you: “blocked”, “urgent”, “today only”
mobile.message.reason.asks_to_confirm_da: It asks you to “confirm” or update your details
mobile.message.reason.reward_bait: It promises a payout, a prize or compensation
mobile.message.reason.call_unknown_numbe: It asks you to call a number that isn't an official one — a real bank or agency doesn't do that
mobile.message.reason.link_not_official: The link doesn't lead to an official website
mobile.message.reason.link_shortener: A short link hides where it really leads
mobile.message.reason.link_messenger: The link opens a messenger chat, not a website
mobile.message.reason.link_ip_address: The link has numbers instead of a website name
mobile.message.reason.link_lookalike: Letters in the website name are swapped — it only looks like the real one
mobile.message.reason.link_imitates_bran: The website name imitates a well-known company
mobile.message.reason.link_apk: The link downloads an app file (.apk) — a common way to plant a virus
mobile.message.reason.asks_for_code: It asks you to tell someone a code from an SMS
mobile.message.reason.safe_account: It tells you to move money to a “safe account”
mobile.message.reason.asks_for_payment: It asks you to pay — a fine, a fee, a charge or a “duty”
mobile.message.reason.relative_in_troubl: Someone writes as a relative or friend and asks for money
mobile.message.reason.install_app: It asks you to install an app
mobile.message.reason.malware_lure: It lures you into opening a “photo” or “video” — a common way to spread viruses
mobile.message.reason.sms_transfer_comma: It asks you to send an SMS command that transfers money
mobile.message.reason.disguised_letters: Words are written with swapped letters to get past filters
mobile.message.reason.sender_personal_nu: An organisation is writing from an ordinary mobile number
mobile.message.reason.sender_mismatch: The sender isn't who the message claims to be
mobile.message.reason.asks_for_secrecy: It asks you to keep the message or the call secret, even from family
mobile.message.reason.text_resembles_sca: The wording is very close to known scam messages
mobile.message.shape.login_code: This looks like an ordinary login code. Never tell this code to anyone — not even a “bank employee”.
mobile.message.shape.payment_alert: This looks like an ordinary payment notice from a bank. If you didn't make this payment, call the bank on the number on your card.
mobile.message.shape.pickup_code: This looks like an ordinary parcel pickup code. Give it only at the pickup point or to the courier when you collect the parcel.
mobile.message.shape.public_alert: This looks like an official public alert, for example from the emergency services.
mobile.message.shape.safety_notice: This looks like a warning about scammers from a bank or a mobile operator.
mobile.message.link.blocked: On our list of scam sites
mobile.message.link.allowed: Not checked: you allowed this site yourself
mobile.message.link.system: Not checked: a shared service like Google — anyone can put a page there
mobile.message.link.shortener: Short link — you can't see where it leads
mobile.message.link.messenger: Opens a messenger chat — we can't check who is on the other end
mobile.message.link.dangerous: Dangerous site, according to our check
mobile.message.link.clean: Our check found no problems with the site
mobile.message.link.rate_limited: Not checked: too many checks in a row. Try again in a few minutes.
mobile.message.link.timeout: Not checked: our server didn't answer in time
mobile.message.list_missing: The list of scam sites isn't on this phone yet, so the links weren't compared with it. The list downloads while the “Every app” shield is on.
mobile.message.list_server_ios: On iPhone, the site names from these links are checked on Cleanway's server — never the text or the full address.
mobile.message.list_stale: The list of scam sites on this phone hasn't been updated for a while. It updates while the “Every app” shield is on.
mobile.message.advice.no_link: Don't open the link from this message.
mobile.message.advice.no_reply: Don't reply, and don't call the numbers in it.
mobile.message.advice.no_code: Never tell anyone a code from an SMS — banks, the police and government services never ask for it.
mobile.message.advice.no_money: Don't transfer or pay money because a message asked you to.
mobile.message.advice.no_install: Don't install anything from the link.
mobile.message.advice.call_yourself: Not sure? Call the bank yourself on the number on the back of your card — other organisations on the number from their official website.
mobile.message.advice.call_relative: Call your relative back on the old number you know.
mobile.message.truncated: The message is very long — only its beginning was checked.
mobile.message.error_failed: Something went wrong. This does not mean the message is safe — please try again.
mobile.message.error_unsupported: Checking messages isn't available on this phone. You can still check a link from it: Share → Cleanway.
mobile.message.privacy: The text is checked on this phone only and is not sent anywhere. History keeps only the result and the website names, never the text. To check a link, only the website name and a random install number that changes every day go to our server.
mobile.breach.title: Leaked password check
mobile.breach.subtitle: Some people use their email address as their password. This tells you if that has already leaked.
mobile.breach.scope_note: This is not a full breach report. Listing every breach an address was caught in needs a paid data source we have not connected yet.
mobile.breach.found_body: This address has turned up in lists of leaked passwords (times found: {{times}}). If you use it as a password anywhere, change that password now.
mobile.breach.clear_body: This address has not turned up as a password in any leak we can see. It may still have been in a breach we cannot check.
mobile.breach.error_body: The check did not go through. Please try again in a minute.
mobile.breach.how_step_1: Your email is turned into a long code on this phone.
mobile.breach.how_step_2: Only the first 5 characters of that code are sent.
mobile.breach.how_step_3: The server sends back hundreds of codes that start the same way.
mobile.breach.how_step_4: Your phone finds the match on its own.
mobile.breach.privacy: Your email address never leaves this phone.
mobile.history.score_hint: A higher score means more risk.
mobile.history.empty_body: Every link you check shows up here. The list is kept on this phone only.
mobile.history.privacy: This list stays on your phone. When you check a link, only the website name and a random install number that changes every day are sent to our servers.
mobile.history.filter_hint.all: Everything Cleanway stopped or warned you about, and everything you checked yourself.
mobile.history.filter_hint.blocked: Sites Cleanway didn't let open, and dangerous links you checked yourself.
mobile.history.filter_hint.warned: Sites Cleanway warned you about, and links you checked that call for care.
mobile.history.filter_hint.checked: Links and messages you checked yourself.
mobile.history.filter_hint.sms: Messages you checked. The text itself is never saved — only the result and the website names.
mobile.history.truncated: Only the most recent events are shown.
mobile.history.empty_on_body: Protection is on. When Cleanway stops a dangerous site, it will show up here.
mobile.history.empty_off_body: Cleanway isn't blocking dangerous sites right now, so there's nothing here. Turn protection on and blocked sites will show up here.
mobile.history.empty_warned_body: Sites Cleanway warns you about, and links you check that call for care, will show up here.
mobile.history.empty_checked_body: Paste a link or share it to Cleanway — the result will show up here.
mobile.history.empty_sms_body: Share a suspicious SMS to Cleanway or paste its text. The text itself isn't saved — only the result.
mobile.history.detail.blocked_body: This site is on the list of scam sites — Cleanway didn't let it open.
mobile.history.detail.blocked_calm: You don't need to do anything: the site didn't open.
mobile.history.detail.warned_body: The link had already opened when the check showed that this site looks like a scam.
mobile.history.detail.warned_advice: If the page is still open, close it and don't type anything on it. If you already entered a password or card details, call your bank on the number on the back of your card.
mobile.history.detail.allowed_body: You marked this site as not a scam — Cleanway doesn't block it.
mobile.history.detail.allowed_removed_bo: Earlier you marked this site as not a scam. It is no longer in your allowed sites, so Cleanway blocks it again.
mobile.history.detail.allow_confirm_body:
If someone on the phone is asking you to allow a site, it's a scammer. Hang up.

Allow {{domain}} only if you yourself are sure it is the real site. Cleanway will stop blocking it. You can undo this in Settings → Allowed sites.
mobile.history.listed_a11y: On the list of scam sites
mobile.report.title: Weekly report
mobile.report.summary_note: Counted from the links you checked in this app over the last 7 days.
mobile.report.flagged_note: These came back dangerous, or worth a second look.
mobile.report.clean_body: Every link you checked came back clean.
mobile.report.empty_body: Check a link and it will show up here.
mobile.report.share_message: My Cleanway week: {{checked}} links checked, {{flagged}} marked dangerous. cleanway.ai
mobile.report.privacy: This report is built on your phone from the links you checked here. It is not sent anywhere unless you share it.
mobile.score.subtitle: You checked links on {{days}} of the last 7 days
mobile.score.ring_a11y: You checked links on {{days}} of the last 7 days — {{band}}
mobile.score.honesty: This is not a measure of how safe you are. It only counts the days you checked a link in this app.
mobile.score.fact.dangerous_detail: {{num}} of the links you checked this week
mobile.score.empty_body: Check your first link, and this becomes a count of the days you check.
mobile.score.privacy: Worked out on your phone from your own check history. Nothing is sent anywhere.
mobile.settings.sign_in_desc: Keep your settings on all your devices
mobile.settings.signed_in_desc: Signed in. Your settings sync to this account.
mobile.settings.sign_out_confirm_body: Checks and history stay on this phone. Settings stop syncing until you sign in again.
mobile.settings.sign_out_confirm_body_ap: Checks and history stay on this phone. Settings stop syncing until you sign in again. A subscription stays in your account: sign in again to use it on this iPhone.
mobile.settings.plan_desc: Protection on this phone is free
mobile.settings.report_desc: A summary of the links you checked
mobile.settings.family_desc: Send alerts to people you care about, end-to-end encrypted
mobile.settings.skill_note: Used by the Cleanway browser extension to word its warnings. This app does not change its own wording yet. Saved on this phone, and to your account when you are signed in.
mobile.settings.skill_kids_desc: Short, strict warnings, with no button to open a dangerous site anyway.
mobile.settings.skill_regular_desc: The default. Clear warnings with a little detail.
mobile.settings.skill_granny_desc: Simple words, short sentences, no jargon.
mobile.settings.skill_pro_desc: Raw scores, threat types and technical detail.
mobile.settings.alerts_note: Cleanway never reads your clipboard or your SMS — only what you share with it yourself.
mobile.settings.push_desc: Cleanway tells you when it stops a dangerous site.
mobile.settings.auto_check_desc: Share a link or an SMS with Cleanway and it's checked at once. Always on.
mobile.settings.clear_confirm_body: This deletes every check saved on this phone. It cannot be undone.
mobile.settings.data_sources_desc: Majestic Million (CC BY 3.0), Chrome UX Report (CC BY 4.0) and public lists of scam sites
mobile.settings.privacy_note: Your check history stays on this phone. When you check a link, only the website name and a random install number go to our servers. The number changes every day and is there so check limits can count per phone rather than per mobile network.
mobile.settings.sync_failed_body: We couldn't reach your account, so this change won't show on your other devices yet. It will sync next time you change it while online.
mobile.settings.clear_done_body: All saved checks were removed from this phone.
mobile.settings.clear_failed_body: Something went wrong — your history is unchanged. Please try again.
mobile.settings.allowed_desc: Sites you marked as safe. The shield does not block these.
mobile.settings.language_note: Choose the language for the app.
mobile.settings.language_reload_body: Please close and reopen the app to finish switching the layout direction.
mobile.settings.linkguard_note: When on, links you tap in most apps go to Cleanway first; the built-in browsers of Telegram and MAX open links themselves, unchecked. Known scam sites won't open. Other links open straight away while we check the site, and you'll get a warning if the check finds a danger — sometimes this takes up to half a minute.
mobile.settings.linkguard_on_desc: Known scam sites won't open; other links are checked right after they open.
mobile.settings.linkguard_off_desc: Right now links open without a check. Turn this on to check them.
mobile.settings.push_off_desc: Turned off in your phone's settings — you won't hear about blocks. Tap to turn them on.
mobile.settings.linkguard_on_desc_no_lis: Links are checked right after they open; the list of scam sites arrives once you turn on the “All apps” shield.
mobile.family.title: Family Hub
mobile.family.signed_out_body: Sign in to set up Family Hub. When Cleanway blocks a scam in a family member's browser, you get an alert — end-to-end encrypted, so not even Cleanway can read it.
mobile.family.load_failed_body: We couldn't reach our servers, so we can't show your family right now. Your family is still there — please try again.
mobile.family.no_family_body: Get an alert when a scam is blocked in a loved one's browser. End-to-end encrypted — even Cleanway can't read the alerts.
mobile.family.join_invalid: That invite is not valid or has expired. Codes match upper and lower case exactly — pasting is the safest way.
mobile.family.members_load_failed: Couldn't load the member list right now. It usually comes back on its own — check again in a moment.
mobile.family.invite_desc: Makes a one-time code and PIN. Send them by text or read them out. Both appear once — keep them where the other person can read them.
mobile.family.alerts_empty: No alerts yet. When Cleanway blocks a scam in a family member's browser, it shows up here.
mobile.family.alerts_load_failed: Couldn't load alerts right now. This does not mean there are none — please try again.
mobile.family.alerts_undecryptable: {{n}} alert(s) couldn't be read on this phone. They were sent to a key this device doesn't have.
mobile.family.modal_title: Share this with your family member
mobile.family.modal_desc: Both appear once. After this closes you can't see them again — make another invite if you need to.
mobile.family.join_network_failed: We couldn't reach our servers, so the code wasn't checked. Your invite is fine — try again in a moment.
mobile.auth.privacy: With or without an account: we check website names on our servers — never your passwords, messages, or browsing history.
mobile.auth.generic_error: Something went wrong. Please try again.
mobile.auth.not_configured: Sign-in isn't available in this build. You can use everything else without an account.
mobile.auth.otp_sub: Enter your email and we'll send you a login code
mobile.auth.code_sub: We sent a sign-in code to {{email}}
mobile.auth.err_code: Enter the code from the email
mobile.auth.err_code_wrong: Wrong or expired code. Request a new one.
mobile.auth.err_network: No connection. Check your internet and try again.
mobile.auth.err_rate_limited: Too many code requests. Please wait a little and try again.
mobile.auth.err_captcha: The security check didn't finish. Please try again.
mobile.auth.err_captcha_update: Signing in needs a newer version of Cleanway. Please update the app and try again.
mobile.auth.code_valid_for: The code is valid for 10 minutes.
mobile.auth.code_spam_hint: No email? Give it a minute and check your Spam folder. The sender is Cleanway.
mobile.auth.password_sub: This account signs in with a password.
mobile.auth.err_password_rate_limited: Too many sign-in attempts. Please wait a few minutes and try again.
mobile.onboarding.s1_title: Check anything before you tap it
mobile.onboarding.s1_desc: Paste a link, scan a QR code, or share anything suspicious straight to Cleanway. You get a plain answer and the reasons behind it.
mobile.onboarding.s2_desc: To check a link, our servers get the website name and a random install number that changes every day. Your passwords, message texts and full page addresses never leave your phone.
mobile.onboarding.s3_desc: On Android, one setup step blocks known scam sites in every app. Brand-new scams can slip past any blocklist — that's what the check button is for.
mobile.onboarding.s3_desc_ios: Cleanway is getting a Safari extension, a scam-text filter and DNS protection for iPhone. They arrive in updates, and the home screen shows what's ready. Today you can check anything in one tap, or with Share → Cleanway.
mobile.android_native.fg_channel_desc: Shown while phishing protection is active
mobile.android_native.block_channel_desc: Tells you when Cleanway blocks a dangerous site
mobile.android_native.allow_channel_desc: Where to allow a site Cleanway blocked
mobile.android_native.allow_moved_text: Sites can now be allowed only in the Cleanway app. If someone on the phone is asking you to allow a site, it's a scammer. Hang up. If you yourself are sure {{domain}} is the real site, tap here to open History.
mobile.android_native.blocked_text: {{domain}} is on the list of scam sites. It won't open.
mobile.android_native.warn_title: This site looks like a scam
mobile.android_native.warn_text: {{domain}} looks dangerous. If it is open, close it and don't type anything.
mobile.android_native.paused_text: Turns back on by itself at {{time}}.
mobile.android_native.caution_channel_de: Quiet notices: a site that looks like a scam, repeats and the summary. No sound.
mobile.android_native.summary_text: Cleanway keeps blocking. The full list is in History.
mobile.android_native.after_call_text: {{reason}} If the caller asked for a code, a transfer, opening a site or installing an app — it's a scam. Don't transfer anything and don't tell anyone a code.
mobile.android_native.after_call_reason_: During the call, or right after it, Cleanway stopped a dangerous site.
During the call, or right after it, a site that looks like a scam opened.
During the call, or right after it, you checked a dangerous message.

mobile.call_guard.title_in_call: You are on the phone right now
mobile.call_guard.title_after_call: You were on the phone a moment ago
mobile.call_guard.body_in_call: If you are being asked to switch protection off, open a site or install an app — it's a scam. Hang up.
mobile.call_guard.body_after_call: If the caller asked you to switch protection off, open a site or install an app — it's a scam. Don't do it, and don't call back on a number the caller gave you.
mobile.call_guard.proceed_wait: I understand, this is my call ({{seconds}})
mobile.call_guard.proceed: I understand, this is my call
mobile.call_guard.proceed_hint: Wait a few seconds. If in doubt — hang up.
mobile.call_guard.honesty: Cleanway does not identify numbers, does not block calls and does not listen to conversations. Who is calling is shown by your mobile operator.
mobile.call_guard.demand_title: A call from your bank, the police or a government office?
mobile.call_guard.demand_body: Hang up. A real bank never asks for a code from an SMS, a transfer to a “safe account”, switching protection off or installing an app. Call your bank back yourself — on the number on the back of your card.
mobile.call_guard.home_button_sub: What to do when the bank or the police call
mobile.reason.flagged_dangerous: Google flags this site as dangerous
mobile.reason.on_blocklists: On trusted scam and spam blocklists

mobile.account.title: Account
mobile.account.free_desc: Blocking known scam sites is always free
mobile.account.status_past_due: The payment didn't go through — please update your payment method
mobile.account.devices_note: A device is a phone, tablet or browser signed in to this account. Unlink one you no longer use and its place frees up at once.

mobile.account.unlink_failed: Couldn't unlink the device. Please try again.

mobile.ios_sms.line_ready: Moves scam texts from unknown senders to Junk, right on this iPhone. Works once you turn it on in Settings.
mobile.ios_sms.sheet_lead: Only you can switch on an SMS filter, in iPhone Settings. iPhone doesn't tell Cleanway whether it's on, so this row stays here as a reminder.
mobile.ios_sms.step_screen: Scroll down to Unknown Senders and turn on Screen Unknown Senders.
mobile.ios_sms.step_choose: Tap Text Message Filter and choose Cleanway. It stays grey until Screen Unknown Senders is on.
mobile.ios_sms.screen_note: Screen Unknown Senders moves messages from numbers that aren't in your contacts into a separate list: in Messages, tap Filters, then Unknown Senders. Verification codes still notify you by default.
mobile.ios_sms.older_ios: On iOS 18: Settings → Apps → Messages → Unknown & Spam → SMS Filtering → Cleanway. On iOS 17 and earlier: Settings → Messages → Unknown & Spam → SMS Filtering → Cleanway.
mobile.ios_sms.note_what: Only texts that are clearly a scam go to Junk (Messages → Filters → Junk). Doubtful ones stay in your inbox.
mobile.ios_sms.note_privacy: The check runs on your iPhone. The text of a message never leaves the phone — not even to Cleanway.
mobile.ios_sms.note_limits: iPhone shows the filter only SMS and MMS from numbers that aren't in your contacts — never iMessage. If there's no Text Message Filter (SMS Filtering on older iOS), your region or carrier doesn't offer it.
mobile.ios.lead: On iPhone, Cleanway protects you in three ways. Each one gets its setup step here as soon as it arrives in an update.
mobile.ios.lead_ready: On iPhone, Cleanway protects you in three ways. Set up each one below — it takes about a minute.
mobile.ios.safari_line: Warns you right on the page when a site in Safari is a known scam.
mobile.ios.safari_line_on: Working in Safari. Known scam sites get a warning right on the page.
mobile.ios.safari_line_off: Turned off in Safari's settings. Tap Set up to turn it on.
mobile.ios.safari_line_allow: Turned on. Now allow it on other websites, then open any site in Safari.
mobile.ios.safari_line_setup: Two switches in Settings, about a minute. Tap Set up for the steps.
mobile.ios.safari_setup_step1: Open Settings → Apps → Safari → Extensions → Cleanway. (On iOS 17 and earlier: Settings → Safari → Extensions.)
mobile.ios.safari_setup_step3: Under Permissions, tap Other Websites and choose Allow (on older iOS: All Websites).
mobile.ios.safari_setup_step4: Tap Test it in Safari below, then come back. When this card says On, Safari is protected.
mobile.ios.safari_setup_why: Why all websites: a scam site is usually one you have never opened before, so Cleanway has to be allowed everywhere to warn you in time. Safari shows its note about reading web pages, passwords and card numbers for every extension that works on websites.
mobile.ios.sms_line: Moves scam texts from unknown senders to Junk. Apple never lets it see iMessage or texts from your contacts.
mobile.ios.dns_line: Blocks known scam sites in every app, through an encrypted DNS setting you approve in iPhone Settings.
mobile.ios.dns.title: DNS protection
mobile.ios.dns.privacy_body: On iPhone the check happens on Cleanway's server, not on the phone as on Android. While DNS protection is on, your iPhone sends the name of each site an app opens (like example.com — never the full link or the page), encrypted, to Cleanway's DNS server. The server blocks names on the scam list and asks Cloudflare's DNS for the address of the rest. Cleanway doesn't record which sites you open: the server writes no log of the names, keeps only totals such as how many sites it blocked, and remembers recent answers in memory by the site name alone, never by who asked. Our hosting provider keeps its standard request logs (privacy policy, section 11).
mobile.ios.dns.step_add_body: Saves the setting on your iPhone. It stays off until you choose it in Settings.
mobile.ios.dns.step_on_body: Open Settings, then General → VPN & Device Management → DNS, and tap Cleanway.
mobile.ios.dns.status_turn_on: Added. Now choose Cleanway in Settings — this screen updates when you come back.
mobile.ios.dns.status_on: On. Your iPhone looks up sites through Cleanway.
mobile.ios.dns.note_off: If sites stop opening, choose Automatic in the same DNS setting, or remove Cleanway below.
mobile.ios.dns.note_other_dns: While another app that changes your iPhone's connection or DNS is on, your iPhone may use that app's DNS instead of Cleanway's.
mobile.ios.dns.error_status: Couldn't read your iPhone's DNS settings. Close this and try again.
mobile.ios.dns.error_add: Your iPhone didn't save the setting. Try again; if it keeps failing, update Cleanway.
mobile.ios.dns.error_remove: Your iPhone didn't remove the setting. You can remove it in Settings → General → VPN & Device Management → DNS.
mobile.fallback.not_found_body: It may be meant for a newer version of the app. Update Cleanway, or go to the home screen.
mobile.fallback.error_body: This screen couldn't be shown. Go back to the home screen and try again from there.
